Periods of weak late night scattered showers and otherwise isolated 
showers will continue through Friday. Unstable air ahead of current 
Invest 95W, currently located over the Marshall Islands, will bring a
slight chance of thunderstorms for the rest of the forecast period 
starting Friday night. Shower coverage looks to become more scattered
on Independence Day as precipitable water values increase across the
Marianas ahead of 95W. Heavy showers will become more widespread 
Sunday and Monday and flooding could be a risk for areas with the 
heaviest rainfall which will depend on the track of current Tropical
Depression 09W. Winds are expected to build gradually beginning late
Friday night or early Saturday and could become damaging by Sunday 
depending on the track and intensity of 95W. This situation remains 
uncertain and will continue to be monitored closely. Refer to the 
Tropical Systems section below for more details on Invest 95W.

Marine...
Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet and light to gentle trade winds are 
expected through Friday for the Marianas. The main swell is the east-
northeast trade wind swell. There will be a moderate risk of rip 
currents along east facing reefs through Friday night. Scattered 
showers are expected late tonight and Thursday night. By Friday 
night, a slight chance of thunderstorms will be possible through the 
weekend and into early next week. Shower chances look to start 
increasing Saturday and by Sunday, tropical storm conditions are 
possible through at least Monday. Seas are expected to start building
Saturday, July 4th as swell from current Tropical Depression 09W 
approaches the Marianas. Seas may become hazardous to small craft as 
soon as Saturday night. This situation will continue to be monitored 
closely.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 95W was upgraded to a TCFA (Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert)
around 11 PM ChST last night, then upgraded further to Tropical
Depression (TD) 09W at 1 PM ChST this afternoon. This system is
currently located 345 miles east-northeast of Pohnpei and tracking 
west (275 degrees) at 10 knots (12 mph). 09W is forecast to continue 
strengthening tonight, possibly becoming a tropical storm Thursday as
it moves toward the Marianas, potentially moving through the island
chain sometime late this weekend through early next week. However, a
large spread amongst the operational models and their ensemble 
members places that track anywhere from near the southern tip of Guam
to Pagan in the northern CNMI. 

Additionally, all model guidance indicates a favorable environment 
characterized by low wind shear (perhaps briefly medium between 48 
and 60 hours out. As noted in the JTWC (Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
who issues the official forecast tracks and cyclone strength/rating) 
Prognostic Discussion, this modest increase in wind shear will be 
brief as a ridge of high pressure coming off the coast of China 
links up with a subtropical ridge centered north-northeast of the 
Marianas. Given warm and deep sea surface temperatures of 29-30 deg 
C., rapid strengthening is possible upon TD 09W's approach. With 
that said, how long would this occur (if it occurs), when and where, 
and what impact on tropical cyclone strength will it have remains an 
good question.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the 
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Tropical Depression 09W continues to move slowly west at 12 mph, as
it's currently located just southeast of Ujelang in the RMI, or 
roughly 345 miles east-northeast of Pohnpei. Pohnpei, Kosrae, and 
Majuro have been removed from the heavier rainfall and "inflow" into 
the storm. However, Pohnpei and Kosrae may still see "fringe effects"
with brief periods of locally heavy showers and an isolated wind 
gusts near 25 knots possible through the next 24 to 36 hours. Then as
we head through the remainder of the week and into the first half of
next week, the NET looks to meander in place, with periods of 
increased rainfall potential. However, specifics on timing and 
probabilities will become better defined once 09W strengthens more, 
and the modified synoptic pattern takes hold, along with NET (the 
Near-Equatorial Trough) alignment, as it will be a key "player" for 
helping focus embedded surface trough movement/trajectories.

Mariners can expect periods of gentle to moderate winds becoming more
light to gentle with time at Pohnpei and Kosrae, remaining light to
gentle at Majuro. Seas will hold in the 4 to 6 foot range, with the
potential for a light westerly to northwesterly swell to develop by
the weekend (if not sooner).
